review_text_raw:
I don't write many reviews and this one is more of a warning in some ways. 

This is much more of a click along adventure with a couple of mini games. I haven't replayed the game to see if the solutions to the mini games are random or fixed. But i purchased the game after playing the demo and that definitely felt like the game would involve much more gameplay and hard work, perhaps some red herrings and a chance to fail.

It is hard to give a proper review of the game without ruining it for people, but it is very short. The slow delivery of text communications or waiting on videos to play pads it out considerably at times and it does feel deliberate to lengthen the game especially at times when there is tension and i personally felt i would be doing things much faster if i had been allowed.

Now don't take that the wrong way, i suspect most people who complain it is short were wanting more. Even if you work out the twists before they come it is worth getting to the end, though it does feel a bit disappointing when you already worked out the big reveals early on. And yes if you look carefully you will at least suspect very early in the game what some outcomes will be. 

Over all the game concept and execution is good, i would have preferred more puzzles or having to dig a bit more for solutions to problems, you are given tools you use exactly once and then never have to use again. It feels set up for a sequel and i hope that they do make one with a longer story.

If you are looking for a click along movie and enjoy that type of game then it may be worth full price to you.
If you are looking for a complex puzzle game where you are the one solving things wait till it is on sale but still get it.

review_text_raw:
Let's start with the obvious as soon as you start the game : the sound design, musics, sound effects, ambiance and voice acting are *gorgeous*. And it gets better with time.

Yet I'm debating to put a thumb up or down. On the one hand, it's original and well made with an impressive level of finition. On pretty much every aspect.
On the other hand ... I don't believe a game is the proper vector for this experience. The gaming aspects constantly break the immersion (at least for me), which in turn ruin any tension or engagement towards the plot, as I view it from a game point of view. For instance, you're in a conversation with someone, yet can take the time to do whatever background checks you want and the person will kindly wait as long as you want before you answer. All of this make the events less impactful emotionnally. I'd add to that a deep insatisfaction with the ending (not as much the content of it as the unfinished business that stops abruptly), and the frustration of sometimes not doing the things right, but still having to deal with the consequences. Yes, it's more immersive, but it makes the gaming experience more frustrating, and I don't want to restart the whole game, so I have a feeling of unfinished business. Not in a branching story game way, more like losing a level but having to go on instead of restarting.

To sum up in a single sentence : the gaming aspects are in the way of the immersion, and the immersion is in the way of the gaming enjoyment.

+++ Sound design
++ Global quality and realism
+ A few good ideas and tools thrown into the mix for variety
- The end, with multiple untied ends
- Too short, with a lack of reusability of the tools and 'sandbox' aspect (you're very handheld at all times)
-- The inadequate mix of immersion and gaming

I'm not the sharpest and usually spam the hint button in these type of games, despite this I only asked for help once trying to find a certain badge for a code. The puzzles make you think, but not frustrate you with their complexity.
 
There were two things that I didn't like at all in this game, one being the ending. Even though I did everything right, I still got the bad ending with no satisfying end. The other problem being the big plot twist. As soon as I heard about the COLE family, combined with the files with the 100 names, and the intro cutscene, I basically already knew what the great reveal was going to be. It should've been hidden better, at least until the research facility part of the story.
 
Finally, I do wish there was more build up, that you complete some "filler" tasks before the whole conspiracy story begins. The progression felt a bit too fast for my taste, I would've enjoyed getting a few calls from agents who ask for help, not related to the story. Still this is one of those games where the story hooked me so bad I wished there was a movie of it. Definitely buying the sequal as soon as it's released.

Here's the bad news first: This game is maybe 3-4 hours long. The puzzles aren't too terribly hard to figure out and there doesn't seem to be any branching paths to the narrative. Also, the blur effect on the cutscenes could be irritating to some.

The good news: It's a well-told story that IS short, but it's surprisingly punchy. A few of the puzzles are gripping to solve and the story builds consistently with intrigue and suspense as you go. It's all organic and nothing feels out of place. The soundtrack is *superbly* done with music fitting pretty much everything you're doing. 

$14 for 3 hours is kind of a steep ask for a video game, but considering how much it is to go to a movie theater these days and spend more for *less*, your mileage may vary. Worth it on a sale, I'd wager.

Give this one a look! The ending definitely has some hints to a possible sequel and if they make one, I have faith they'll make an even longer game with more to do as this feels almost like a tech demo or a trial run. I want them to really sink in a longer story, more intrigue, more stuff to do, and give us the chance to find a better path than just one single narrative. 

Choice matters to the player and if we feel like nothing we did really changed anything on the main scenario, it can be jarring when the ending piledrives us with how things turned out despite our efforts. Food for thought, Bureau 81!

Anyways, I'm giving this a recommend. Your choice to wait for sale or not, but it's not so steep you won't enjoy yourself with a well-crafted and thought-out experience. Light on gaming, heavy on story and immersion.
